title: Partial Vs Full Range of Motion Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
publication: International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
population: Studies comparing partial and full range-of-motion training on hypertrophy, strength, sport, power and body-fat outcomes; participant details are not summarized in the abstract.
key_findings: Overall the difference was trivial, slightly favouring full range of motion (standardized mean difference 0.12, interval -0.02 to 0.26); every outcome group favoured full range by a trivial to small amount.
A subgroup suggested a possible hypertrophy benefit of partial range performed at long muscle lengths over full range, with an interval that includes no difference.
Strength gains were specific to the range trained, and partial range may be a reasonable choice for variation, preference or when injury prevents full range.
methods: Pre-registered systematic review following PRISMA with a Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis and exploratory subgroup and moderator analyses.
limitations: The long-muscle-length subgroup estimate is uncertain and exploratory; differences overall are trivial to small. Not indexed in PubMed; verified against Crossref only.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by on 2026-11-25.
